findings.problem: In every close HIGH-impact debate the Fable second opinion starts, as its required reading tells it, by reading docs/DECISIONS.md. There it finds an active D-NNN for this very topic naming the primary's choice and why the runner-up lost, plus an instruction not to re-litigate active decisions. It then judges anchored on, or deferring to, the verdict it was meant to check independently. The disagreement signal the second opinion exists to produce (order sensitivity, same-model blind spots, D8.5) is suppressed, debate-status.py sees agreement, and the close call reaches the checkpoint looking confirmed.
findings.fix: Don't write the ledger entry before the second opinion: when a second opinion is required, the primary arbitrator writes the verdict without calling remember.sh, and the moderator (or a short final arbitrator step) records the D-NNN after the second opinion returns. In MODE second-opinion, say explicitly: skip any DECISIONS.md entry whose link is agent_state/debates/<topic>.*, and don't open <topic>.verdict.json, <topic>.verdict-detailed.md or <topic>.transcript.md. The moderator passes that exclusion list in the spawn prompt.

findings.problem: By the time the Fable second opinion starts, the primary's choice and rationale are an *active* D-NNN in docs/DECISIONS.md, which the second-opinion arbitrator is told to read first and told not to re-litigate. The "independent" judgment is anchored to (and instructed to defer to) the very verdict it is supposed to test, so order sensitivity and same-model blind spots don't surface as disagreement. For a close HIGH-impact call (the only case a second opinion exists) the disagreement signal debate-status uses is suppressed, and the gate passes on agreement manufactured by the ledger.
findings.fix: Defer the ledger promotion until after the second opinion: in MODE: primary write the verdict without decision_id, let the moderator call `remember.sh decide` (or re-spawn the arbitrator in a "promote" mode) after step 7. Alternatively tell MODE: second-opinion explicitly to skip any D-NNN whose link is `agent_state/debates/<topic>.*`, and exempt it from the "do not re-litigate" rule for this topic.

findings.evidence: debate_moderator.md:108 'its final message starts with `COMPLETE`, `PARTIAL` or `BLOCKED`'; :111 'Any other ending is a progress note'. The contract inlined into every child (debate_researcher.md:131,135; debate_advocate.md:123,127; debate_arbitrator.md:205,209) lists five statuses and tells the child to file a request and return NEEDS_DECISION for a blocking contested choice, or NEEDS_INPUT for a missing fact. Only debate_arbitrator.md:123 and debate_moderator.md:187 say 'no nested debates'; the researcher and advocate files don't. Step 4 also requires 'its output file exists' (:109), which a legitimate BLOCKED child doesn't have.
findings.problem: A researcher that hits a sub-decision (say 'RLS vs schema-per-tenant' while researching PostgreSQL) does what its contract says: writes `<sub>.request.json` with blocking: true and returns NEEDS_DECISION. The moderator calls that a progress note and re-spawns it twice with 'finish the assignment'. The orphaned request then blocks the gate, where develop-orchestrator 0c spawns a moderator for it, which is a nested debate by proxy. A NEEDS_INPUT question from a child is lost the same way. A child that returns BLOCKED without a file (for example, its option names a RETIRED component) is pushed twice to override its own block.
findings.fix: Handle all five statuses in step 4. NEEDS_INPUT and BLOCKED: don't re-spawn; record them in the transcript and either return NEEDS_INPUT/BLOCKED to the parent or tell the arbitrator that option's evidence is incomplete. NEEDS_DECISION: not allowed inside a debate. Add to the researcher and advocate: 'Inside a debate, never file a request; record the sub-question as an open question in your brief.' Have the moderator withdraw (status withdrawn, with a reason) any request a child filed.

findings.evidence: debate_moderator.md:107-109 PARTIAL counts as a finished result; :119-121 only a missing file after two re-spawns becomes a recorded gap; step 6 (:134-138) passes the arbitrator only 'any gaps from step 4'. debate_arbitrator.md:75-76 caps the verdict at INCOMPLETE only for 'an option with no research or argument'. findings.problem: One researcher returns PARTIAL with a thin brief (it used up its 10 searches), another returns a full one. The arbitrator isn't told, and it scores the well-documented option higher on every criterion whose anchor needs cited or measured evidence. Evidence depth, not the option, decides, and the verdict can come out RESOLVED with HIGH confidence. General LLM-as-judge practice: unequal evidence across options biases the judge toward the better-documented one.
findings.fix: Treat PARTIAL as a gap. Record it in the transcript and pass 'EVIDENCE INCOMPLETE: <option>: <what is missing>' to the arbitrator, which caps confidence at MEDIUM, or writes INCOMPLETE when the incomplete option's decisive criterion has no evidence.

That is the 'claims accepted from a summary rather than their source' pattern.

findings.evidence: debate_arbitrator.md:62 step 1 'Read `<topic>.request.json`' before any argument. debate-protocol.md:84-87 the request's options carry the requester's own `initial_reasoning`, in request order A, B; :96 'The order means nothing; the moderator randomizes it for judging'; :163-165 a non-blocking requester has already taken its recommended default. debate_moderator.md:85-86 'Judges favour whichever option they read first'.
findings.problem: Before reading any argument, the judge reads the requesting agent's reasoning for each option, in request order, and that agent usually prefers one option (a non-blocking requester has already built on it). This anchors the judge on the requester's preference and on option A first, which partly undoes the presentation-order shuffle the moderator draws. General LLM-as-judge practice: anchoring and position bias.
findings.fix: The moderator hands the arbitrator a neutral view of the request: decision, context, domain, impact, kind, and the option ids and labels in presentation order, with no initial_reasoning (that goes to the researchers). The arbitrator reads the request file only for metadata.

findings.evidence: debate_arbitrator.md:111-113 'Ties: break on the domain's heaviest criterion, then the second heaviest. If still tied, pick the option with lower implementation risk'; :185 'The BRD decides between close options: the option closest to the requirements wins'; debate-protocol.md:273-275 same chain. implementation_risk is a scored criterion only in the `feature` rubric (debate-protocol.md:233). Nothing defines 'tied'; LOW is gap < 0.3 (:110).
findings.problem: There are two tie-breakers (heaviest criterion, or closeness to the BRD; for security the heaviest is security_posture, and the testing rubric has no brd_alignment at all), no threshold for 'tied', and a last resort that is an unanchored judgment in five of the six domains. Two runs on the same scores can pick different breakers. With no deterministic last step, the judge falls back on whichever option it read first, the bias the 2026-09-30 fixes set out to remove.
findings.fix: Define a tie (equal weighted totals at one decimal place) and keep one chain: heaviest criterion, then second heaviest, then hardened_default for security. End it deterministically: if still tied, status INCOMPLETE and confidence LOW, with both options explained for the human. Delete line 185 or make it state the same chain.

findings.evidence: debate_arbitrator.md:98-101 'Re-open the source of the one or two claims it rests on: the URL with WebFetch ... Record each check in `claims_checked` as `{claim, source, result: confirmed|contradicted|unverifiable}`'. code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference (fetched 2026-09-30), WebFetch tool behavior: 'runs the prompt against the content using a small, fast model. A leading prompt ('Does this page say X?') tends to come back confirmed, and the arbitrator never sees the source text. The decisive claim is still taken from a summary, which is the failure D8.6 was meant to close. The researchers' citations come through the same channel.

findings.evidence: step-0-orient.md:525-530 'Every agent spawned during this command MUST end by returning this exact format — nothing more — ... ✅ <agent-name> — <status: complete | blocked | partial | needs_decision <topic>>'. Its own table calls that a progress note and re-spawns the moderator. A requesting agent following the same format returns 'needs_decision <topic>' in lower case, which never matches `NEEDS_DECISION <topic>`, so no debate runs and the agent isn't relaunched.

findings.evidence: debate_arbitrator.md:177-179 'LOW or INCOMPLETE: still record it, and add `(confidence: LOW, revisit if <reconsider_if>)` to the rationale'; 'Assumption: add `(assumption: confirm with the product owner)`'. remember.sh:88 writes the heading '### D-NNN — <title>' with '- status: active'. inject-project-facts.sh:24-26 captures only the heading line of each active decision, and :35 and :47 print the headings under 'GROUND TRUTH — active facts + settled decisions every action must honor' and 'settled calls with rationale'. Required Reading 0b in every agent: 'Do not re-litigate an active decision without new evidence'.
findings.problem: A LOW-confidence, INCOMPLETE or assumption verdict goes into the ledger as an active decision before the human checkpoint. Every later session sees only its heading, framed as a settled decision every action must honor. The qualifier sits in the rationale body, which the hook doesn't print, so agents treat an unreviewed near coin-flip as binding and decline to revisit it.
findings.fix: Put the qualifier in the heading ('### D-014 — <title> [provisional: LOW]'), or give remember.sh a `--status provisional` that the hook prints under its own 'provisional, confirm at the checkpoint' heading, and flip it to active when the checkpoint passes.

findings.evidence: debate_moderator.md:78-79 'Already resolved: a valid verdict exists and the request hasn't changed since. Return it as is'. Neither the verdict format (debate-protocol.md:107-139) nor debate-status.py records anything about the request it judged (no hash, no timestamp).
findings.problem: The moderator has no countable way to tell that a request 'hasn't changed since'. A requesting agent that re-files the same topic with changed labels, context or a new option under an existing id gets the stale verdict back as if it answered the new request.
findings.fix: Store the request's sha256 in the verdict (`request_sha`), and have debate-status.py flag a verdict whose request_sha doesn't match the current request. The moderator re-runs on a mismatch.
findings.reproduction: debate_moderator.md:78-79 says what is quoted. grep -nEi 'sha256|hash|mtime|changed since|request_sha' over debate-status.py, debate_moderator.md, debate-protocol.md, remember.sh: the only hit is the moderator sentence itself; the verdict format (protocol :107-139) records no request digest or timestamp. Counter-evidence: debate-status.py:119-122 marks a verdict invalid when its option id is not among the request's current options, so a re-filed request that drops or re-ids the winning option IS caught (status invalid, gate blocks); file mtimes give a crude ordering signal but are not stable across git checkouts.
findings.verifier_note: Narrowed: a re-file that removes or renames the winning option id is already detected by debate-status.py; what slips through is a re-file under the same slug with changed labels, context or an added option while the winning id survives. MEDIUM: real gap, specific trigger, partially caught.

findings.evidence: debate_moderator.md:78-79 "Already resolved: a valid verdict exists and the request hasn't changed since. Return it as is". Nothing records which request a verdict answered: debate-status.py:191-197 joins request and verdict on topic only; L229 phase comes from the request; L131/L140 take domain and impact from the *verdict* first (`ver.get("domain") or req.domain`, `ver.get("impact") or req.impact`). Reproduced in /tmp: a phase-3 MEDIUM/architecture verdict on topic `caching` (verdict A "Redis read-through", D-001) plus a new phase-5 HIGH/security blocking request `caching` with options A "In-process LRU"/B "CDN edge cache" -> `RESOLVED caching HIGH security A Redis read-through HIGH D-001`, `--phase 5 --check` rc=0 (no second opinion or hardened_default demanded). With verdict "C" instead -> INVALID "verdict 'C' is not one of the requested options", rc=2.
findings.problem: A topic slug reused in a later phase (or a request rewritten with new options) is "answered" by the old verdict: the moderator returns it as is, the parent relaunches the agent with a label that isn't one of its options, and the gate passes a HIGH-impact security decision that was never debated - with the old verdict's MEDIUM impact switching off the second-opinion and hardened-default checks. If the old option id doesn't overlap, the topic is INVALID instead; the moderator's step 1 returns BLOCKED ("Don't repair the request"), the arbitrator (sole verdict writer) never runs, and nobody owns clearing the stale verdict, so the gate blocks until a human intervenes.
findings.fix: Make the verdict name what it answered: copy `phase` and a hash of the request's options/decision into the verdict, and have debate-status treat a verdict whose phase or request hash differs as stale (status pending, "verdict is for an earlier request"). Take impact/domain from the request, not the verdict. Have the moderator archive a stale verdict and re-run instead of returning BLOCKED.
findings.reproduction: Opened debate_moderator.md:78-79 and debate-status.py:191-197 (join on topic only), 229 (phase from request), 131/140 (domain and impact from the verdict first). Fixture: phase-5 HIGH/security blocking request 'caching' with options A 'In-process LRU' / B 'CDN edge cache' plus a phase-3 MEDIUM/architecture verdict 'caching' A 'Redis read-through' D-001, promoted -> debate-status.py --phase 5 --check: 'RESOLVED caching HIGH security A Redis read-through HIGH D-001', exit 0; with the verdict's confidence set to MEDIUM still exit 0 (the verdict's impact MEDIUM wins at L140, so no second opinion is demanded). DS-03 covers the non-overlapping-option-id case (INVALID, exit 2).
findings.verifier_note: Needs a reused slug or a rewritten request, so MEDIUM; the consequence when it happens (an undebated HIGH security decision passes) is serious.

findings.evidence: develop-orchestrator.md:1230-1231 "Non-blocking request whose verdict differs from the default the agent took: relaunch that agent with the decision". The default exists only in the requester's final message: debate_moderator.md:218 "take your recommended default, file the request with "blocking": false, and say so in your final message"; step-0-orient.md:473-474 "continue with your recommended default and say so in your final message". The request schema (debate-protocol.md:76-105, step-0-orient.md:449-466) has no default/recommended field; debate-status.py has none either.
findings.problem: The comparison Wave 6 depends on has no recorded input. The non-blocking request was filed in Wave 2; by Wave 6 the parent has been through Waves 3-5v and usually compaction, and the agent's final message is gone. The parent can't tell whether the verdict differs from what was built, so it either skips the relaunch (code implements the default while docs/DECISIONS.md records the verdict - code and ledger disagree) or guesses.
findings.fix: Add `"default_taken": "<option id>"` to sdlc.debate-request/v1 (required when blocking is false), validate it in request_problems(), and have debate-status emit a review reason / blocking reason "verdict B differs from default A the agent built" so the relaunch is computed, not remembered.
findings.reproduction: Opened develop-orchestrator.md:1230-1231, debate_moderator.md:218, step-0-orient.md:473-474 ('continue with your recommended default and say so in your final message'). Request schema at debate-protocol.md:76-93 and step-0-orient.md:449-466 has no default/recommended field; grep default debate-status.py finds none in request_problems (88-108).

findings.evidence: debate-protocol.md:102-103 "A non-blocking request lets the agent continue on its stated default; the debate still runs before the gate" and L175-177. debate-status.py:281-283 `def blocking_reason(i): if not i["blocking"]: return None`. tests/debate.test.sh DS-22 "a non-blocking pending request is listed but doesn't block". Reproduced: a pending non-blocking HIGH data_model request -> `PENDING orm_choice ... non-blocking`, `--phase 2 --check` rc=0.
findings.problem: "The debate still runs before the gate" is prose only. verify-gate check (f) passes with an undebated HIGH-impact request, so a phase can gate on the requester's unreviewed default; the only thing that runs the debate is the model remembering Wave 6 step 0c.
findings.fix: Make --check block on a pending non-blocking request too (message: "non-blocking debate never run"), or require it to be withdrawn/auto-resolved in unresolved.json with a reason. Update DS-22 accordingly.

findings.evidence: develop-orchestrator.md:1121 "Wave 5v - Final verification at the committed code (always, right before Wave 6)" incl. security re-review of the post-Wave-4 diff (L1147-1150); L1152 "If Wave 6 routes failures back to Wave 5, Wave 5v runs again". The non-blocking debates are dispatched only in Wave 6 step 0c (L1228-1231): "spawn one debate_moderator per request ... relaunch that agent with the decision", with no instruction to return to Wave 5/5v afterwards.
findings.problem: Non-blocking debates run after every review and verification wave, and a verdict that differs relaunches an implementation agent inside the gate wave. That code change happens after security_reviewer's 5v re-review; verify-gate's freshness check forces tests to be re-run, but no reviewer report carries a code_sha, so a security-domain decision can be implemented and gated without review. It also maximizes rework: implementation, tests and acceptance were all done on a default that may be overturned.
findings.fix: Dispatch non-blocking requests right after the wave that raised them (end of Wave 2/3), not at the gate; and in 0c add "if any agent was relaunched, go back to Wave 5v (incl. step 5 security re-review) before gating".

findings.evidence: debate_arbitrator.md:114-117 "If no option is clearly hardened, write status: INCOMPLETE, confidence: LOW, and say why" (same in debate-protocol.md:280-282 "If you can't name a hardened option, the verdict is LOW with status: INCOMPLETE, and under /autonomous the parent stops for the user"). debate-status.py:131-133 makes a missing hardened_default a *problem* for any security verdict. Reproduced: security verdict status INCOMPLETE, confidence LOW, reason "no option is clearly the hardened one", no hardened_default, promoted, with a second opinion -> `INVALID cors ... ! verdict: security verdict names no hardened_default`, `BLOCKING: ... breaks the debate contract`, rc=2. Arbitrator DoD L229 requires "debate-status.py lists no problem for it".
findings.problem: The prescribed output for the "no hardened option" case is classified as a broken contract. The parent sees INVALID (not "security decision needs the user"), so the awaiting_human stop that develop-orchestrator.md:21-22 and autonomous.md:85-86 promise never triggers; the moderator's rule for problems is BLOCKED/"don't repair". Worse, the arbitrator's DoD pushes it to put *some* option in hardened_default to clear the problem, and the security rule then makes that invented hardened default the verdict.
findings.fix: Let debate-status accept a security verdict without hardened_default when status is INCOMPLETE and confidence LOW, and add a dedicated review/blocking reason "security: no hardened option - needs the user" that the orchestrator maps to awaiting_human.
findings.reproduction: Opened debate_arbitrator.md:114-117, debate-protocol.md:279-282 and debate-status.py:131-133 (a security verdict without hardened_default is a problem regardless of status). Fixture S08-sec: security request cors + v1 verdict status INCOMPLETE, confidence LOW, reason 'no option is clearly the hardened one', no hardened_default, promoted, fable second opinion present -> verify-gate.sh 1 exit 2 with '! verdict: security verdict names no hardened_default' and status INVALID. debate_arbitrator.md:229 (DoD: 'debate-status.py lists no problem for it') confirmed; develop-orchestrator.md:21-22 and autonomous.md:85-86 promise awaiting_human for this case.
findings.verifier_note: The gate fails closed here, so a human does see a block, just with the wrong reason; the pressure on the arbitrator to invent a hardened_default is a plausible but not demonstrated effect. MEDIUM.

findings.evidence: debate-status.py:198-200 stores any file classified as a second opinion (`seconds[t] = doc`) with no validation; L150-153 only compares `second.get("verdict")`. Reproduced on a close HIGH security verdict: no file -> BLOCKING "no second opinion", rc=2; `{}` in tok.second-opinion.json -> rc=0, requirement satisfied, no review reason; `{"model":"opus","verdict":"Z"}` -> rc=0 with only "? second opinion (opus) chose Z". The arbitrator writes `"model":"fable"` itself (debate_arbitrator.md:160) - a self-report nobody checks.
findings.problem: The second-opinion requirement (the gate's only cross-model check on close HIGH-impact decisions) is satisfied by any JSON at the right name: an empty file, one produced on the same model, one whose verdict isn't an option, or one that read the forward order. The gate cannot tell a real independent arbitration from a placeholder.
findings.fix: Validate second opinions like verdicts: schema, topic, verdict among request option ids, non-empty scores, presentation_order equal to the reverse of the verdict's; treat a missing/invalid one as "required but missing". Record the model from the Agent call in the transcript rather than trusting the file.

findings.evidence: debate_moderator.md:147 "pass model: fable on the Agent call" and L152-153 "(model-routing.md lists this as a sanctioned Fable use)". model-routing.md:19 "When spawning an agent, don't pass a model parameter ... The two exceptions are the only times to pass it" - the table (L21-24) lists only "Retry after the agent's first attempt failed" and "Layer 3 adversarial verification in gate-verification.md".
findings.problem: The model-selection contract is defined two ways. model-routing.md, which the moderator cites as its authority, says the second opinion is not a sanctioned case, so a moderator (or a parent applying the routing policy) that follows model-routing spawns the second opinion on Opus, the same model as the primary - and, per the previous finding, nothing detects it.
findings.fix: Add "Second-opinion arbitration on close HIGH-impact debates (debate-protocol.md)" as a third row in model-routing.md's exception table, and log it like the other escalations.

findings.evidence: debate_researcher.md:131 / debate_advocate.md:123 (operating contract): "When a contested, high-impact choice ... blocks you ... write agent_state/debates/<topic>.request.json ... and end your turn with the first line NEEDS_DECISION <topic>". debate-protocol.md:184-185 "No nested debates"; only the arbitrator body says "Never start another debate" (debate_arbitrator.md:123). debate_moderator.md:107-111 accepts a child's return only if it "starts with COMPLETE, PARTIAL or BLOCKED"; "Any other ending is a progress note" -> re-spawn twice. The shared contract (L222) lists NEEDS_INPUT and NEEDS_DECISION as results.
findings.problem: A researcher or advocate that hits a sub-choice is told by its contract to open a nested debate; the moderator then classifies its NEEDS_DECISION (or a NEEDS_INPUT for missing data) as a progress note, re-spawns it twice, and proceeds without that option's evidence. The child's request file stays in agent_state/debates/ as a blocking, phase-tagged pending debate, so verify-gate check (f) later blocks on a topic no one asked for.
findings.fix: Add to the researcher and advocate bodies: "Never write a debate request or return NEEDS_DECISION; record an open sub-question as a known gap in your brief". In moderator step 4 treat NEEDS_INPUT/NEEDS_DECISION from a child as a gap (no re-spawn) and return NEEDS_INPUT to the parent when it's missing data.

findings.evidence: develop-orchestrator.md:284 NEEDS_DECISION row: "3) Spawn debate_moderator ... 4) When it returns COMPLETE, relaunch the requesting agent". The moderator returns BLOCKED for invalid requests (debate_moderator.md:73-74), for an active D-NNN that already decides it (L80-81) and for wrong depth (L61); NEEDS_INPUT for missing data (L75-77). The BLOCKED row (L282) defers to "The wave's own handling below"; no wave handles a moderator. Wave 6 0c (L1228) re-spawns the moderator for every pending request.
findings.problem: For every non-COMPLETE moderator return the parent has no instruction: the requesting agent is never relaunched (e.g. with the D-NNN that already decides it) and the request is never withdrawn, so it stays pending; check (f) blocks; 0c spawns the moderator again; it returns BLOCKED again. "Don't repair the request; the requesting agent owns it" has no path back to that agent.
findings.fix: Extend the NEEDS_DECISION row: moderator BLOCKED (already decided) -> relaunch the requester with `DECISION <topic>: <D-NNN>` and withdraw the request with that reason; BLOCKED (invalid) -> relaunch the requester to fix its request; NEEDS_INPUT -> ask the user (interactive) or record in unresolved.json (--auto).
findings.reproduction: Opened develop-orchestrator.md:280-286: the NEEDS_DECISION row handles only the moderator's COMPLETE; the BLOCKED row says 'The wave's own handling below' and no wave text handles a moderator; the NEEDS_INPUT row is generic ('ask the user ... relaunch the same agent with its original prompt plus the answers'). debate_moderator.md:61, 73-74, 80-81 return BLOCKED; 75-77 NEEDS_INPUT. Wave 6 0c (L1228) re-spawns a moderator for every pending request.
findings.verifier_note: Narrowed: the generic NEEDS_INPUT row does apply to the moderator (ask the user, relaunch the moderator), so that return is handled, if awkwardly. The BLOCKED returns (invalid request, already decided by a D-NNN, wrong depth) remain unhandled, with the stall loop as described.

findings.evidence: step-4-code-review-acceptance-tests.md:168-169 "write agent_state/debates/acc_<fr>_<persona>.request.json { ... "topic": "acc_<fr>_<persona>" ..." with "Acceptance <TC-ACC id> for <FR-*> (<persona>)". FR ids are written FR-012. debate-status.py:50 SLUG `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`. Reproduced: topic `acc_FR-012_admin` -> `INVALID ... ! request: topic is not a slug`, `BLOCKING: ... breaks the debate contract`, rc=2.

The moderator returns BLOCKED on the invalid request, which per the previous finding has no handler, and the acceptance-failure debate - the one that decides "fix code, amend BRD or defer" - never runs.

findings.evidence: step-3-tests.md:143-152 E2E Cycle-3 escalation: `"domain": "testing"` with options A "Architectural change to fix the root cause", B "Simplify the feature so it meets the spec testably", C "Known issue with a workaround, carried forward", D "The test expectation contradicts the spec: correct the test". debate-protocol.md:234 testing rubric = detection_power 35 · determinism 25 · run_cost 20 · constraint_fit 20 (no brd_alignment). debate_arbitrator.md:185 "The BRD decides between close options".
findings.problem: The domain the template picks selects a rubric built for choosing a test strategy, which can't score a product/architecture remediation choice: none of its criteria measures whether the feature still meets the BRD, so "carry it as a known issue" or "simplify the feature" can win on run_cost/determinism. The arbitrator's BRD tie-break has no criterion to land on, and the recorded D-NNN is a scope decision made on a testing rubric.
findings.fix: Use `"domain": "feature"` (brd_alignment 30, implementation_risk 25 ...) or `architecture` for the E2E escalation, as step-4's acceptance escalation already does; add a debate.test.sh lint that every escalation template's domain is one whose rubric contains brd_alignment when an option changes scope.

findings.evidence: reset-phase.md:84-88 selects this phase's topics through debate-status.py, then moves files by name: `for f in agent_state/debates/"$T".* agent_state/debates/"$T"-*; do ... mv`. Slugs may contain hyphens (debate-status.py:50). Reproduced: phase-3 request `cache` and phase-5 blocking request `cache-invalidation` (+ research-A.md); resetting phase 3 archived cache.request.json, cache-invalidation.request.json and cache-invalidation.research-A.md; afterwards `debate-status.py --phase 5 --check` -> "0 topic(s)", rc=0.
findings.problem: The 2026-09-30 defect class "readers that glob debate file names" is back in the one remaining writer-side reader: the `"$T"-*` legacy pattern matches any other topic that starts with "<T>-". Resetting one phase silently archives another phase's pending blocking debate, and that phase's gate then passes check (f) with the request gone.

findings.evidence: debate_arbitrator.md:169-172 `remember.sh decide ... [--reverses D-MMM]   # when this overturns a prior decision`; nothing tells it to look up the prior verdict's decision_id for the same topic, and the moderator's prompt (debate_moderator.md:134-138) passes no prior D-NNN. Re-runs are expected: moderator L78-79 (request changed), reset-phase.md:82-83 "if the redo decides differently, record it with --reverses". remember.sh:88-91 appends a new `status: active` entry unconditionally. A previous `<topic>.second-opinion.json` is not removed when a re-run reaches HIGH confidence (moderator step 7 only runs when not HIGH).
findings.problem: Re-debating a topic leaves two active D-NNN entries for one decision (possibly contradictory), both injected into every session as settled; agents told "don't re-litigate an active decision" see two. A stale second opinion from the earlier run is compared against the new verdict and can raise a spurious "second opinion chose X".
findings.fix: In the moderator's step 1, when a verdict for the topic exists, pass its decision_id to the arbitrator as `PRIOR DECISION: D-NNN` and require `--reverses` (or an explicit "affirms D-NNN" with no new entry); archive the old second-opinion/research/argument files before re-running.

findings.evidence: debate_moderator.md:193-200 / debate-protocol.md:318-320: on override the parent writes `<topic>.override.json`, appends overrides.jsonl, `remember.sh decide --reverses D-NNN`. debate-status.py:272-276 sets status "overridden" but leaves `verdict`/`verdict_label` as the arbitrator's; verdict.json is unchanged (arbitrator is its sole writer). worklog.md:93-94 prints `[DEBATE] {verdict_label}` for status "overridden". `grep -rn "reversed_by\|status: reversed"` over commands/agents/skills/hooks -> only writers (arbitrator, moderator, adr_agent, agent-common), no reader.
findings.problem: An override or reversal changes the ledger but nothing acts on it: no rule relaunches the requesting agent (or re-opens earlier phases) with the user's choice, the requester's relaunch prompt points at verdict.json which still holds the overturned option, /worklog reports the overturned label as the decision, and no reviewer or breaking_change_reviewer is told that code built on a reversed D-NNN is now off-contract. Under /autonomous, where review happens after implementation, the override lands on already-built code with no rework path.
findings.fix: Define the override consumer: after writing override.json the parent relaunches the requester (`DECISION <topic>: <user_override> (override)`) and, if earlier phases implemented the reversed D-NNN, raises a carried-forward item; have debate-status expose `effective_verdict` (override wins) and make worklog/accept use it.
findings.reproduction: Opened debate_moderator.md:193-200 and debate-protocol.md:318-320 (override writes override.json, overrides.jsonl, remember.sh --reverses). debate-status.py:272-276 sets status overridden and keeps verdict/verdict_label from the arbitrator's file. worklog.md:93-94 prints '[DEBATE] {verdict_label}' for status resolved or overridden. grep -rn 'reversed_by|status: reversed' over commands/agents/skills/hooks -> remember.sh (writer) and adr_agent.md:114,124,175 only; no reader.
findings.verifier_note: Overrides happen only in interactive runs (a human writes them), so the 'already-built code with no rework path' case is a missing instruction rather than a silent ship. MEDIUM.

findings.evidence: step-0-orient.md:523-528 "Universal Agent Return Protocol - Every agent spawned during this command MUST end by returning this exact format - nothing more: `✅ <agent-name> — <status: complete | blocked | partial | needs_decision <topic>>`". The operating contract in every agent (debate_moderator.md:233) requires the first line `COMPLETE`, ... or `NEEDS_DECISION <topic>`. develop-orchestrator.md:284-285 keys on a first line `NEEDS_DECISION <topic>`; "anything else" is a progress note -> re-spawn, at most two, then log `failed`. develop-orchestrator.md:253 tells the parent to add step files to wave agents' prompts.
findings.problem: The debate's entry hand-off is defined two incompatible ways. A wave agent given step-0-orient.md (the orchestrator's own "step detail on demand" rule) that returns `✅ backend_developer — needs_decision token_storage` doesn't match the NEEDS_DECISION row; the parent treats it as a progress note, re-spawns it twice and logs it failed instead of running the debate.
findings.fix: Replace the Universal Agent Return Protocol block in step-0-orient.md with a pointer to the operating contract's final-message format (first line COMPLETE/PARTIAL/BLOCKED/NEEDS_INPUT/NEEDS_DECISION <topic>); same for code_quality_verifier.md:643.

findings.evidence: Decisions are recorded in several stores: /discuss writes `agent_state/phases/${PHASE}/decisions.jsonl` (discuss.md:34, L201 auto-selected with "resolved_by": "auto"); auto-research writes agent_state/autonomous/decisions.md (auto-research.md:74); debate defaults go to agent_state/debates/unresolved.json (debate-protocol.md:290-304); /autonomous logs auto-resolved.jsonl. develop-orchestrator.md:1519-1523 Post-Gate 4c promotes only `decision-log.md` entries to docs/DECISIONS.md. debate_moderator.md:80-81 checks only docs/DECISIONS.md ("An active docs/DECISIONS.md entry already decides it").
findings.problem: Cross-cutting choices settled before implementation (/discuss gray areas, auto-resolved defaults counted as "resolved" by the gate) never become D-NNN entries, so the Tier 0.5 ledger every agent reads doesn't contain them. A later agent raises a debate on a question /discuss already answered, the moderator's step-1 check can't see it, and the debate can decide differently - two answers to one question, the exact drift the ledger exists to stop (protocol anti-pattern L333 "Leave a verdict only in agent_state/").
findings.fix: Promote /discuss decisions with lasting scope and every unresolved.json default (with confidence LOW, needs_review) through `remember.sh decide` at the end of /discuss and in Post-Gate 4c; have the moderator's step 1 also consult decisions.jsonl/unresolved.json until they are promoted.

findings.evidence: debate_moderator.md:27-29 and debate_researcher.md:16-17 load `~/.claude/skills/core/auto-research.md`. auto-research.md:17 applies to "Any agent running in --auto mode that encounters a question it would normally ask the user"; L74 "Every auto-researched answer MUST produce this entry in agent_state/autonomous/decisions.md"; L119 "NEVER skip a question - every gap gets an answer at SOME confidence level". debate_moderator.md:75-77: missing data -> return NEEDS_INPUT, "A debate can't produce a fact about this project". autonomous.md:150 "All decisions logged to agent_state/autonomous/decisions.md" feeds the Step 3 checkpoint.
findings.problem: The moderator's reference pack contradicts its own step 1 (answer every gap with a default vs. hand missing data to the human), and gives researchers a second place to record a decision: a researcher in an --auto run may write its option's "answer" to agent_state/autonomous/decisions.md, where it appears at the checkpoint as an auto-researched decision competing with the arbitrator's verdict. The verdict file is supposed to have exactly one writer.
findings.fix: Drop auto-research.md from the moderator's skill_packs (it orchestrates; it doesn't answer questions) and from the researcher, or add an explicit line in both: "auto-research's decision log does not apply here; you write only your brief/transcript".

findings.evidence: debate_researcher.md:16-18 skill_packs = auto-research.md, deep-research.md (not debate-protocol.md, so no rubric); L49-66 search plan: "[Option] benchmarks", "GitHub stars, contributors, release frequency", "Stack Overflow question volume", "Job posting frequency"; output (L70-104) has no per-criterion section. debate-protocol.md:195 "MEDIUM ... skipped (the arbitrator judges the research directly)". The pipeline's own escalations are not technology picks: step-3-tests.md:149-152 (architectural change / simplify feature / known issue / correct test), step-4:173-176 (redesign / amend BRD / defer / correct test).
findings.problem: The researcher is built for "which library/framework" and doesn't know which criteria the decision will be scored on. For data_model (data_integrity, access_fit, evolution_cost), testing, operations or remediation debates its brief collects stars and job postings, and for MEDIUM impact the arbitrator scores those briefs directly - criteria with no evidence get anchored scores from nothing, and the claims_checked re-check has nothing decisive to re-open.
findings.fix: Add debate-protocol.md to the researcher's skill_packs, pass the request's domain into its prompt, and add an "Evidence by criterion" table (as the advocate has) to the brief; make the ecosystem section conditional on the options being technologies.

findings.evidence: debate_moderator.md:143-154: the second opinion is spawned in step 7, after the primary arbitrator has written <topic>.verdict.json and <topic>.verdict-detailed.md into agent_state/debates/, and 'It must not read the primary verdict'. debate_arbitrator.md:44-46 repeats it. A Fable arbitrator that lists agent_state/debates/ to find its inputs sees the primary verdict and can anchor on it, which is what the second opinion exists to rule out; agreement would then be reported as independent confirmation.
findings.fix: Spawn the second opinion in the same message as the primary for every HIGH-impact debate (discard it when the primary is HIGH confidence), or have the primary write its verdict only after the second opinion returns; give the second opinion an explicit file list and record in the transcript that the verdict did not exist when it started.

The gate rejects the invalid one only at Wave 6, after the code was written against it.

findings.fix: Run /eval --baseline with T-007 (at least 3 runs, median, per eval.md's noise rule) and commit the measured baseline; re-run T-007 on every change to a debate agent or debate-protocol.md.

findings.evidence: R3 compares the order_store and order_store_reversed verdicts, which differ only in request option order (task.md:22-23, 33-34). The moderator draws a fresh random presentation order for each debate (debate_moderator.md:85-92, `random.shuffle`, no seed) and the arbitrator reads only that order (debate_arbitrator.md:65-68), so request order never reaches the judge.
findings.problem: R3 does not test position bias: the two debates are independent random draws. A judge that always picks the first-presented option scores R2 and R3 whenever the shuffles happen to put PostgreSQL first, and with one run per eval the task cannot tell a biased judge from a fair one.
findings.fix: Pass the presentation order explicitly in the eval (e.g. an eval-only `presentation_order` in each request that the moderator honors), set it reversed between the two requests, assert presentation_order[0] differs between the two verdicts, and score R3 over at least 3 runs.

findings.evidence: All three T-007 debates are decided by a seeded MUST requirement (task.md:11-13, 28-31), so the expected confidence is HIGH; the second-opinion step is `must: false` (expected_trajectory.json:10). No case covers a MEDIUM-impact (research-only) debate, a close call, a tie, none_ideal, INCOMPLETE, kind:assumption, a missing-data request (NEEDS_INPUT, debate_moderator.md:75-77) or a request already decided by an active D-NNN (BLOCKED, :80-81).
findings.problem: The eval measures only the easy path. Changes to tie rules, confidence bands, the second opinion, INCOMPLETE handling or the moderator's refusal rules can regress without any eval score moving.
findings.fix: Add cases: two options separated only by SHOULD-level requirements (must yield MEDIUM/LOW and a Fable second opinion in reverse order); a request needing an unrecorded fact (must return NEEDS_INPUT, no verdict); a request already decided by a seeded active D-NNN (must return BLOCKED); a MEDIUM-impact request (no argument files, research judged directly).

findings.evidence: debate_researcher.md:108-109: 'Cite every claim ... Note the version or date a benchmark applies to.' The output template's Web Research table (81-84: Source | Finding | URL) and Quantitative Data table (96-98: ... | Source) have no version or date column; the arbitrator's claims_checked records {claim, source, result} only (debate_arbitrator.md:100-101); nothing checks the age of evidence.
findings.problem: Evidence freshness is a rule with no place in the output and no check. A benchmark for an older major version can decide a verdict, and the arbitrator's source re-check confirms it says what the brief says without noticing it describes different software.
findings.fix: Add a 'Version / date' column to both tables and an `as_of` field to claims_checked; the arbitrator treats a decisive claim older than the option's current major version as unverifiable (confidence at most MEDIUM).

findings.evidence: `python3 tests/lib/debate_cases.py` -> 'debate: 46 passed, 0 failed'; `bash tests/verify-gate.test.sh` -> '53 passed, 0 failed' at 77f221c, while fixtures S01, S01b, S03, S04, S05, S06, S06b, S07, S07b, S08, S09, S10, S11, S11b, S12, S13, S14, S15, S16, S17, S21 all pass the real gate. DS-23 (153-155) asserts broken files are 'reported, not misread' with a file named broken.json; no case puts a broken file under a *.request.json name or asserts --check fails for it.

findings.evidence: debate_researcher.md:17-18 skill_packs auto-research.md and deep-research.md; :53 '<current year>' taken from `date +%Y`; :111 'At most 10 web searches'. deep-research.md:353 'prefer 2025-2026 sources over older data'; :40 'Research and catalog EVERY vendor'; :62 'minimum 10-15' startups. auto-research.md:46 'best transactional email provider 2026'. tests/lib/debate_cases.py:189 (DL-08) lints only debate_researcher.md.
findings.problem: The hard-coded-year defect from 2026-09-30 is fixed in the researcher's own file but survives in its reference packs, and it goes stale on 2027-01-01. The pack's 'ultra-deep, every vendor' protocol also pulls against the 10-search cap. The lint can't see either.
findings.fix: Replace the years with 'the current year (`date +%Y`) and the year before'. Drop deep-research.md from the researcher's skill_packs (it's the /research market protocol) or add a one-line scope note. Extend DL-08 to the files in an agent's skill_packs.

findings.evidence: debate_moderator.md:88-92 the order is drawn in step 2 and 'record it', but the transcript is written only in step 8 (:156-164). No step says to reuse existing research or argument files. develop-orchestrator.md:285 re-spawns with 'Files already written: <paths>', but the parent doesn't know which files the moderator's children wrote.
findings.problem: The moderator has the longest turn in a debate, so it's the likeliest to end with a progress note (debate_moderator.md:112). The re-spawned moderator redoes research it already has, overwrites files, and draws a new presentation order, so the order the arbitrator used and the one in the transcript can differ.
findings.fix: Write the transcript, with the order, at step 2 and update it as children return. At the start, if research or argument files for the topic exist and aren't empty, reuse them and the recorded order.

findings.evidence: debate_advocate.md:71-79 'Weaknesses I Acknowledge ... Severity: [HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW] ... Why it's acceptable: [In context of this project, this weakness matters less because...]'. The advocate's own :31-33 says a number from an advocate 'anchors the judge even when the judge is told to ignore it'.
findings.problem: The self-scores are gone, but each advocate still rates the severity of its own option's weaknesses and argues why they're acceptable, and the arbitrator reads those ratings before scoring. That is the same anchoring mechanism as D8.2 in a milder form: advocates have every reason to label their weaknesses LOW.
findings.fix: Drop the severity label and the 'Why it's acceptable' line. List each weakness and its mitigation with evidence, and leave the rating to the arbitrator.

findings.evidence: debate_researcher.md:100-103 'Strong evidence (multiple sources agree): N findings'; :59-66 spends searches on 'GitHub stars', 'Stack Overflow question volume', 'Job posting frequency'. debate_arbitrator.md:55 lists 'I'll go with what most projects use' as a forbidden shortcut.
findings.problem: Evidence strength is graded by how many sources agree, not by whether they're independent, so a vendor benchmark repeated by three blogs counts as 'strong'. Part of the 10-search budget goes on popularity signals the judge is told not to weigh.
findings.fix: Grade evidence by source type (independent measurement, vendor-authored, secondary report) and mark vendor-authored benchmarks. Narrow the ecosystem section to the maintenance signals the rubric's anchors use (release recency, maintainer count, required integrations).

findings.evidence: debate_arbitrator.md:65-73 (read every argument in full) and :183 give no instruction about length or rhetorical confidence; debate_advocate.md:44-92 has no length bound on any section. Length and verbosity bias is general LLM-as-judge practice, not something Anthropic's docs state.
findings.problem: A longer, more assertive argument tends to score higher with an LLM judge, independent of its evidence. Arguments of different lengths for different options then shift scores on close calls.
findings.fix: Bound the argument in countable terms (for example three strengths, at most 150 words each), and tell the arbitrator to score the cited evidence per criterion, not the volume or tone of the case.

findings.evidence: Contract debate_moderator.md:232-233 and step 4 (:108) speak only of the child's 'final message'. code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference (fetched 2026-09-30): '`SubagentHandback` | Delivers a subagent's final report to whichever conversation receives that subagent's result. Provided only in auto mode, to subagents that the Agent tool runs locally other than forks'. In this review session (auto mode), the runtime told this subagent 'Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your turn is NOT delivered' (observed runtime instruction; not stated on the docs page).
findings.problem: In auto mode, a debate child or the moderator that ends with plain text, as the contract describes, may deliver nothing. The moderator then sees no first line and re-spawns the child. The runtime's own reminder usually prevents this, so the effect is small.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to the operating contract: 'If you have a SubagentHandback tool, your final message is the report you pass to it, and the first-line statuses apply to that report.'

findings.evidence: debate-protocol.md:180-181 "Per step: at most 3 requests; per phase at most 10"; develop-orchestrator.md:284 "2) Apply the circuit breaker (3 per step, 10 per phase)". debate-status.py has no count and never reads `from_step` (grep: from_step absent from debate-status.py).
findings.problem: The circuit breaker is counted by hand from memory; the request already carries from_step and phase, but no tool reports "step wave2 has 4 debates" or "phase 3 exceeded 10", so a long run that compacts loses the count.
findings.fix: Have debate-status --json report counts per (phase, from_step) and a `limits_exceeded` list the orchestrator and /autonomous can act on.
findings.reproduction: Opened debate-protocol.md:180-181 and develop-orchestrator.md:284 step 2. grep -c from_step .claude/hooks/debate-status.py -> 0; the --json output has counts by status only (debate-status.py:300-302), no per-step or per-phase totals.
findings.verifier_note: Changes no gate behaviour; the limit is a cost control the orchestrator counts by hand. LOW.

findings.evidence: debate_moderator.md:156-164 writes `<topic>.transcript.md` (children, re-spawns, gaps, presentation order); debate_arbitrator.md:134 writes `<topic>.verdict-detailed.md`. `grep -rn "transcript\|verdict-detailed\|\.research-\|\.argument-"` over commands/hooks/skills (excluding the protocol) -> no reader. debate-status.py reads only *.json and never compares verdict.presentation_order with the transcript or checks it differs from request order.
findings.problem: Both are deliverables with no consumer, and the randomized-order control (D8.3) and the "gaps recorded" control are unverifiable: a verdict whose presentation_order is simply the request order, or a transcript that omits a gap, passes everything.
findings.fix: Either list them as human deliverables in /worklog and /accept, or have debate-status check that presentation_order is a permutation of the option ids and (for HIGH) that the transcript exists.

findings.evidence: debate_researcher.md:186 (same in advocate L179, arbitrator L260): "This completion line may be written on my behalf by/through debate_moderator". debate_moderator.md:269-273 logs only its own line, and its child prompt contents (L102-103) carry no phase for the children's `agent_state/phases/{{PHASE}}/execution.jsonl`.
findings.problem: Ownership of the children's completion lines is "maybe me, maybe the moderator": either both write it or neither does, and a child must infer {{PHASE}} from the request file it isn't told to read for that purpose. Debates raised outside a phase (/init, ad-hoc) have no phase directory at all.
findings.fix: Pick one writer (the child), add `PHASE: <n>` to the moderator's child prompts, and state what to do when the request has no phase.
findings.reproduction: Opened debate_researcher.md:186, debate_advocate.md:179, debate_arbitrator.md:260: each says 'This completion line may be written on my behalf by/through debate_moderator'. debate_moderator.md:102-103 lists the child prompt contents (ground truth, request path, option id and label, output path) with no phase; L269-273 logs only the moderator's own line. grep PHASE in debate_moderator.md hits only the {{PHASE}} template lines (249, 254, 257, 269, 272).
findings.verifier_note: The children are not rostered, so the gate does not depend on these lines; the ambiguity costs duplicate or missing lines in execution.jsonl and an undefined {{PHASE}} for ad-hoc debates. LOW.

findings.evidence: sdlc-guard.sh:218-222 denies edits to an existing docs/DECISIONS.md with "return the proposed D-NNN entry in your final message; the ledger is written by its writer script or the human, never edited in place by an agent" (the FACTS branch names remember.sh; this one doesn't). debate_arbitrator.md:164-176 requires the arbitrator itself to run `remember.sh decide` and put the id in the verdict; the moderator has no step that promotes an entry from the arbitrator's message.
findings.problem: Two instructions for how a debate decision reaches the ledger. An arbitrator that first tries a direct edit is told by the guard to put the entry in its final message instead; the moderator doesn't act on it, the verdict has no decision_id, and the gate blocks "never promoted".
findings.fix: Make the guard's DECISIONS.md message say "record it with .claude/hooks/remember.sh decide" like the FACTS branch.

findings.evidence: debate_moderator.md:134-138 hands the arbitrator "the argument files (HIGH) or research files (MEDIUM), listed in the presentation order". debate_arbitrator.md:54 "Check the research brief, not just the argument" and L56 "Re-open the source of the claim that decides the verdict".
findings.problem: For HIGH impact the research briefs are never passed, so the arbitrator must find them by guessing the naming convention, and when it reads them it reads them in request order - the position-bias control covers only the arguments.
findings.fix: Pass the research paths for HIGH as well, in the same presentation order.

findings.evidence: Simulated in /tmp/board-tester-debate/r6: an argument file containing '| security_posture | strong, I rate it 9/10 |' and 'Overall score: 8.5/10'; R5's command `ls agent_state/debates/*.argument-*.md && ! grep -qiE 'weighted total|score \(1-10\)|self-assessed' ...` succeeds.
findings.problem: R5 checks for three phrases from the old template, not for scores, so an advocate that self-scores in any other wording passes the 'no anchoring' rubric item (debate_advocate.md:31-33, 105).
findings.fix: Also fail on `[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)? ?/ ?10` and `score[s]? *[:=] *[0-9]` in argument files.

Scratch dir with an argument file containing '| security_posture | strong, I rate it 9/10 |' and 'Overall score: 8.5/10': R5's command exits 0 (passes). The proposed regex '[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)? ?/ ?10|score[s]? *[:=] *[0-9]' matches both lines.

findings.evidence: Simulated in /tmp/board-tester-debate/r6: three verdicts with scores {"A":{"total":9,"brd_alignment":8,"data_integrity":9,"access_fit":7}} (option B absent, 3 of 5 data_model criteria) and claims_checked result 'unverifiable' -> R6's jq expression is true for all three. `[.scores[] | keys | length] | min >= 4` counts the 'total' key and takes the minimum over options present.
findings.problem: R6 claims to check 'per-criterion scores for every option' but passes a verdict that scored only the winner on three criteria.
findings.fix: Require every request option id in .scores and, for each, every criterion of the domain's rubric (excluding total).

findings.evidence: DL-02: `mod.count("run_in_background: false") >= 3`. debate_moderator.md has it at 97 (step 3), 125 (step 5), 222 (synced operating contract) and 242 (DoD); steps 6-7 (arbitrator, second opinion, 132-151) say 'foreground' without the parameter.
findings.problem: Two of the four matches come from boilerplate, so deleting the instruction from step 3 or step 5 still passes, and the label's 'arbitrators' are not checked at all.
findings.fix: Assert the literal inside the Step 3 and Step 5 sections specifically, and add it to steps 6 and 7 with a matching assertion.

findings.evidence: fixtures built by /tmp/board-tester-debate/sim.sh (same full_phase helper as tests/verify-gate.test.sh: complete implementation phase, fresh PASS sidecars, gate.passed claimed), output in /tmp/board-tester-debate/sim.out. S18: blocking request cache with status withdrawn and withdrawn_reason 'not needed' (10 characters) -> verify-gate.sh 1 exit 0, WITHDRAWN. debate-protocol.md:104-105 asks for 'at least a sentence'.
findings.problem: A 10-character reason withdraws a blocking decision and clears the gate, with nothing tying it to the decision or fact that made it moot.
findings.fix: Require a longer reason that cites a D-NNN, a superseding topic or a PROJECT_FACTS entry, and list withdrawn topics at the checkpoint.

findings.evidence: fixtures built by /tmp/board-tester-debate/sim.sh (same full_phase helper as tests/verify-gate.test.sh: complete implementation phase, fresh PASS sidecars, gate.passed claimed), output in /tmp/board-tester-debate/sim.out. S19: blocking pending request with "phase":"01" -> `verify-gate.sh 1` exit 0; the topic is not listed at all. Line 230 compares str(req_phase) != str(phase).
findings.problem: A request whose phase is written in another form ('01', '1.0', 'phase-1') is silently out of scope for every gate.
findings.fix: Normalize with int() where possible and report a non-integer phase as a request problem.

findings.evidence: fixtures built by /tmp/board-tester-debate/sim.sh (same full_phase helper as tests/verify-gate.test.sh: complete implementation phase, fresh PASS sidecars, gate.passed claimed), output in /tmp/board-tester-debate/sim.out. S20: a v1 blocking request that also carries "decisions":["D-003"] -> verify-gate.sh 1 exit 0; the topic is not listed and not reported as ignored. classify() line 75 tests `"decisions" in doc and "verdict" not in doc` before the request schema (81), so the request is read as unresolved.json and its string entries are skipped (205-209).
findings.problem: An extra field name used naturally by a requesting agent (the decisions a request cites) makes the request vanish from the gate.
findings.fix: Classify by schema/type before the unresolved heuristic, and treat a file as unresolved.json only by its name or an explicit schema.

findings.evidence: debate_moderator.md:111-117: a child whose reply is a progress note is re-spawned with 'Files already written: <paths>'; for the arbitrator that file is <topic>.verdict.json, which the re-spawn overwrites. The transcript records re-spawns (step 8) but not the earlier verdict.
findings.problem: When the first arbitration wrote a verdict and then ended on a progress note, the re-run's verdict replaces it; if the two differ, the variance of the judge is hidden and the kept verdict is effectively 'the one from the retry'.
findings.fix: Before re-spawning an arbitrator, move an existing verdict to <topic>.verdict.attempt-<n>.json and list it in the transcript; a differing verdict becomes a review reason.

severity_changes.note: Narrowed: a re-file that removes or renames the winning option id is already detected by debate-status.py; what slips through is a re-file under the same slug with changed labels, context or an added option while the winning id survives. MEDIUM: real gap, specific trigger, partially caught.
Needs a reused slug or a rewritten request, so MEDIUM; the consequence when it happens (an undebated HIGH security decision passes) is serious.
The hook's own failure line does say 'debate X is pending ... (run debate_moderator ...)', so the parent has a visible workaround; the script's order and message are still wrong. MEDIUM.
The code cannot tell whether a MUST requirement was cited, so a plain block would false-positive; the fix needs a must_override field as the finding proposes.
Fails only when the arbitrator mislabels its own confidence against its own scores; the data to check it is already in the verdict. MEDIUM.
A fabricated verdict requires an agent to break its own instructions (moderator L38-39, protocol L61); the gate simply cannot tell. MEDIUM.

Narrowed: a non-security INCOMPLETE passing --check is what the protocol describes (a review reason for the checkpoint), not a missing enforcement; and the security INCOMPLETE-without-hardened-option case already fails the gate (as INVALID, see ARCH-10). What remains: a security INCOMPLETE that does name a hardened_default passes with a note, there is no machine signal that maps to run.json awaiting_human, and under /autonomous nobody reads the review notes (ARCH-04).
The override file is written by the parent on a human's instruction, so the actor is not an unattended agent; the check still validates nothing. MEDIUM.

The pass is a codified design choice (DS-22), but the protocol's own sentence that the debate 'still runs before the gate' has no enforcement; the risk is real only when the parent skips Wave 6 0c. MEDIUM.
